articles.title: Chevron closes Hess acquisition after winning Exxon legal battle
articles.content: STORY: Chevron sealed the deal for its $55 billion takeover of Hess on Friday, giving the energy giant access to the largest oil discovery in decades.Chevron completed the acquisition after winning a landmark legal battle against its larger rival Exxon Mobil, which had challenged the deal over rights to the Stabroek Block off the coast of Guyana.Exxon argued it had a pre-emptive right to buy Hess' stake in the lucrative offshore oil project, which holds more than 11 billion barrels of oil and is one of the fastest-growing sources of oil in the world.But the International Chamber of Commerce, the court that oversaw the case, ruled in favor of Chevron, and there is no appeals process.Stewart Glickman is an energy equity analyst at CFRA. Now that it's been decided, I think this is a shot in the arm for Chevron's, call it, medium-term production growth prospects because now it has acquired, among other things, the crown jewel, which is Guyana, 30% stake in this offshore oil project that has been throwing off a tremendous amount of production growth over the last couple of years and there are more phases to come that should also drive more incremental growth. Chevron CEO Mike Wirth's strategy to turn around his company's lagging performance hinged on the Hess acquisition, which had been delayed for over a year due to the high-stakes legal dispute.He said in a statement, quote, “This merger of two great American companies brings together the best in the industry.”Reuters previously reported that even as Chevron awaited the arbitration verdict, it was making preparations so it could close the deal with Hess quickly.Wirth said in an interview with Reuters on Friday that converting technology and combining employees from both companies would take a few months.Shares of Chevron were down about a percent in midday Friday trading while Exxon fell more than 3%.
